- Executive Summary: Perplexity has launched the Monitor API, allowing developers to define monitoring goals via natural language for periodic scanning of specific web pages or global information. The service integrates a decision model to filter out noise, pushing verified updates via webhooks only when findings meet predefined criteria for relevance, credibility, and novelty.
- Key Verified Facts:
* [Core Event] Perplexity AI (Enterprise developer ecosystem): Launch of Monitor API for web search and page change monitoring
* [Root Cause & Mechanism] To alleviate the engineering overhead of building custom recurring search pipelines and noise reduction logic
* [Key Metrics] Web monitors cost $1 per 1,000 successful runs, and page monitors cost $1 per 1,000 fetched URLs.
* [Scope & Next Steps] Features include global search monitoring and targeted URL diffing to compete with incumbents like Firecrawl.

- Primary Source: THE DECODER (https://the-decoder.com/hours-after-anthropic-claims-a-claude-proof-of-the-riemann-hypothesis-stanford-releases-an-all-human-competing-draft/)
- Executive Summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a proof for the Riemann Hypothesis using the Claude model, utilizing simulated derivatives. Shortly after, Stanford math professor and AMS president Ravi Vakil released an independent, human-only draft proof by Alessandro Masullo, emphasizing the exclusion of AI assistance.
- Key Verified Facts:
* [Core Event] Levent Alpöge (Anthropic), Alessandro Masullo (Stanford), Ravi Vakil (AMS President): Alpöge presented an AI-assisted proof; Stanford released a purely human-authored competing draft
* [Root Cause & Mechanism] Rising tension over the validity and attribution of AI-assisted mathematical proofs
* [Key Fact Detail] The Riemann Hypothesis serves as a stress test for AI-assisted mathematical reasoning.
* [Key Position & Outlook] Academia counter-positions human-authored work against AI output, intensifying attribution debates.

### New open model Inkling 2 Mini thinks in loops to solve problems with fewer words and still runs on a laptop
- Canonical URL: https://ainewsradar.xyz/news/22084551f26241c2
- Primary Source: THE DECODER (https://the-decoder.com/new-open-model-inkling-2-mini-thinks-in-loops-to-solve-problems-with-fewer-words-and-still-runs-on-a-laptop/)
- Executive Summary: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini, which utilizes a looped transformer architecture where 12 of its 24 layers execute three times to enhance reasoning without increasing token generation. The MoE model features 26.4 billion total parameters with 5.4 billion active per token, supports a 1-million-token context window, and is released under the Apache 2.0 license.
- Key Verified Facts:
* [Core Event] Thinking Machines: Released Inkling 2 Mini featuring looped inference and 1M token context
* [Root Cause & Mechanism] To optimize compute efficiency and reasoning capabilities for small-parameter models in agentic coding tasks
* [Key Metrics] 26.4B total parameters, 5.4B active, with 1M token context window.
* [Key Position & Outlook] Outperforms comparable open-source models on DeepSWE v1.1 and Vals Index v2.2 coding benchmarks.

### Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model
- Canonical URL: https://ainewsradar.xyz/news/441bfa26310d0de1
- Primary Source: THE DECODER (https://the-decoder.com/bytedance-argues-most-ai-training-phases-are-unnecessary-and-backs-it-up-with-a-competitive-open-model/)
- Executive Summary: ByteDance's research team, in collaboration with US universities, argues that contemporary AI agent training pipelines are unnecessarily nested, leading to opaque logic and excessive costs. They demonstrate that only three essential training phases are sufficient for complex task execution and have released an open-source model to validate this streamlined paradigm.
- Key Verified Facts:
* [Core Event] ByteDance research team and US university researchers: Published research on a 3-step training paradigm and released an open-source model
* [Root Cause & Mechanism] To address the bloated, costly, and opaque nature of existing multi-stage AI training pipelines
* [Key Technical Spec] Highlighted the redundancy and high costs of current agent training pipelines.
* [Key Position & Outlook] Validated the efficiency of the new paradigm through an open-source model release.

### The Race to Build a Quantum Computer Has Become a Sprint
- Canonical URL: https://ainewsradar.xyz/news/b5472723360ae54e
- Primary Source: New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/20/science/quantum-computer-neutral-atoms.html?unlocked_article_code=1.R1E.PGHV.x5mP00wlvgC0&smid=nytcore-ios-share)
- Executive Summary: Google has opened a new lab in Colorado to develop alternative quantum computing architectures alongside its existing superconducting qubit program to solve the critical error correction bottleneck. This strategic hedging reflects the escalating race against industry rivals like Amazon, IBM, and Microsoft as the competition shifts from theoretical milestones to practical engineering deployment.
- Key Verified Facts:
* [Core Event] Google Quantum Lab, Hartmut Neven (Physicist): Developing parallel quantum architectures beyond superconducting qubits to address error correction
* [Root Cause & Mechanism] Unresolved error correction bottlenecks and intensified global commercial and state-level competition
* [Key Metrics] In May, after China vowed to pump more than $15.
* [Key Position & Outlook] Global capital influx marks the onset of an intensive commercialization race.
